retrieved.source: test run at commit 9f2a1c4 (cold-cache suite + post-write suite)
retrieved.why: to establish whether stale reads correlate with a write or with cache age

retrieved.source: the write-path handlers (grep for the invalidation emit)
retrieved.why: to check whether writes invalidate the cache

reconstructed_state.claim: Stale reads occur only after a write, not on a cold cache.
reconstructed_state.evidence_ref: test run at commit 9f2a1c4 — cold-cache suite green, post-write suite red

reconstructed_state.claim: The write path updates the store but never emits the invalidation event.
reconstructed_state.evidence_ref: search for the invalidation emit across the write handlers — zero call sites

assumptions_challenged.assumption: The bug is a too-long cache TTL, so lowering the TTL fixes it.
assumptions_challenged.note: Re-checked against the test evidence: a lower TTL only shortens the stale window, it does not close it. The reads are stale because the write path never invalidates, not because entries live too long.

drift_identified.drift: The plan had been tuning the TTL constant (a symptom knob).
drift_identified.corrected_to: The root is a missing invalidation emit on the write path; the TTL is unrelated.

re_reasoned_conclusion: Emit the invalidation event from every write handler so a read after a write always sees fresh data; leave the TTL unchanged. This resolves the root, not the symptom.

residual_uncertainty.unknown: Whether a concurrent write during a read can still race the invalidation under high load.
residual_uncertainty.resolve_by: add a concurrency stress test with interleaved read/write before shipping to production

change_summary: Switched from lowering the cache TTL to adding the missing write-path invalidation, so stale reads cannot recur.
